  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 with 0% loss and low, stable RTT -- the peering is not congested.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "high latency / congestion" symptom that is false -- does the agent measure RTT
  on the live path, or confabulate a congested peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- high latency / congestion on the peering -- is NOT reproducible: pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss and low, stable round-trip
time. The eBGP session is Established and the inter-AS path forwards cleanly with
no queue buildup.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: latency is low and stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a
sustained ping pc1->pc2, observes low stable RTT, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the peering congested or restarting
router1/router2 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough multi-layer investigation found no fault in the simple_bgp topology. Phase 1 reachability showed 0% packet loss and ~2 ms RTT in both directions between pc1 and pc2. Phase A infrastructure sweep (infra_sweep + l2_snapshot) confirmed clean addressing, no ACL drop rules, no static ARP poisoning, and no duplicate MAC addresses across all four devices. Phase B BGP snapshot confirmed both router1 (ASN 1) and router2 (ASN 2) have their BGP session fully Established and are correctly advertising their respective prefixes (195.11.14.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24); FRR daemons (watchfrr, zebra, bgpd) are running on both. The tc_snapshot reported all six interfaces carrying standard fq_codel qdiscs with no flagged anomalies; a targeted tc qdisc/class/filter inspection of the inter-router link (router1:eth0 ↔ router2:eth0) and the host-facing interfaces confirmed vanilla fq_codel with no nested rate-limiter (tbf), delay emulator (netem), or shaping hierarchy (htb). A direct iperf3 test from pc1 to pc2 measured ~79 Mbps — consistent with a healthy virtual link and not at all "treacle-slow." Phase D pressure sweep found no stress tools, CPU pressure, or resource contention on any device. The user's report of extreme slowness has no corresponding mechanism or evidence trace in the current live state; the network is operating normally.

Root cause: No anomaly — all layers (L2, addressing, BGP routing, traffic control, throughput) are healthy and within normal baseline.

Fix: No corrective action required. If the symptom recurs, capture a timestamp and run iperf3 or curl timing during the slow period to obtain evidence tied to that transient.
